questions.prompt: Which race has drawn more outside money so far in the general election?
NO GOING BACK PAC INC. (a super PAC) has spent $345K in SC's 1st District House race. Which party is it helping?
questions.why: Its spending supports the Republican or attacks their opponent. Every group's filings list who it backs or opposes.

questions.prompt: Groups helping Republicans have spent $2.4M in MT's 1st District House race. Are Republicans playing offense or defense?
questions.why: Republicans hold this seat now, so money helping Republicans here is defense.

questions.prompt: Groups helping Democrats have spent $54.6M in the OH Senate race. Are Democrats playing offense or defense?
questions.why: Republicans hold this seat now, so money helping Democrats here is offense.

questions.prompt: A party's coordinated spending in the last three weeks before Nov. 3 is disclosed when?
questions.why: Coordinated spending appears only on regular reports. Anything after Oct. 14 lands on the post-general report, due Dec. 3.

questions.prompt: What's the most one person can give a House candidate for the 2026 general election?
questions.why: The 2025-26 limit is $3,500 per election; the primary and general each count as separate elections.

questions.prompt: In CA's 22nd District House race, outside money favors Democrats by $1.4M. Whose nominee has raised more?
questions.why: Outside money and candidate money point opposite ways here: the Republican leads fundraising by $2.3M.

questions.prompt: A hybrid PAC can do what a super PAC can't. What?
options: Give directly to candidates from a limited account
questions.why: A hybrid PAC keeps two accounts: a limited one for contributions to candidates and an unlimited one for independent spending.
